top_story.headline: Forty-two House Democrats back sanctions on West Bank and Gaza settlements
top_story.dek: The bill from Rep. Joaquin Castro was among 98 measures introduced in a three-minute House session on Thursday, October 1.
paragraphs: H.R. 10642, introduced by Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX-20), would impose sanctions with respect to settlements in the West Bank and Gaza. Congress.gov lists 42 cosponsors, all of them Democrats. The bill was referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the House Committees on the Judiciary, Financial Services, and Ways and Means.
The House met for just three minutes, from 11:30 a.m. to 11:33 a.m., and held no votes. The Senate was in a pro forma session of about 35 seconds. Both chambers return Monday, October 5, 2026.
Among other bills introduced the same day, H.J.Res. 218 from Rep. Steve Cohen (D-TN-9) proposes a constitutional amendment to abolish the electoral college.

sections.headline: A three-minute House session brings 98 new bills and resolutions
paragraphs: On Thursday, October 1, 2026, the House met at 11:30 a.m. and adjourned at 11:33 a.m. with no recorded votes, no Yea and Nay votes and no quorum calls, according to the Daily Digest. The Senate met in a pro forma session at 10:30 a.m. and adjourned 35 seconds later until 4 p.m. Monday, October 5, 2026.

The Daily Digest counts 80 public bills (H.R. 10640–10719), one private bill (H.R. 10720) and 17 resolutions (H.J.Res. 218, H.Con.Res. 122 and H.Res. 1591–1605), 98 in all, listed in full below. Among the most widely cosponsored are H.R. 10642 on West Bank settlements (42 cosponsors) and H.Res. 1603 on book banning (more than 60 listed in the Record). Three voting bills (H.R. 10679, H.R. 10699 and H.R. 10700) were also introduced, as was H.R. 10697 on limits to military use in domestic law enforcement. Most of the rest are routine awareness-month resolutions and narrowly targeted bills.
